analysis: Examined four changes. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md adds two env-var rows (lines 316-317): DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. These are documentation only. Both are performance and scheduling toggles for Qwen MTP, documented as default-on, not forwarded to LaunchAgents, and with no effect on attestation, authorization or crypto. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm is a submodule pointer bump from 19634dd to 3fd6d07. The submodule contents are not supplied, so the underlying MTP decode and carry code cannot be reviewed. The documented behavior covers the Qwen MTP chained decode and prefill hidden-carry paths, which touch TB-007 inference-engine state, and I could not verify KV or carry isolation across requests. This is a coverage limit, not a finding, so needs_deeper_review is true for that submodule. (3) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark.swift is a new benchmark-only public enum in the ProviderBenchmark target. It uses the @_spi(Benchmarking) ProviderCore session. It forces DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=0 in a local environment dictionary passed to makeBenchmarkSession, so it doesn't touch the SSD prefix cache (T-041). It also sets requirePersistentKey: false, with no ephemeral-KEK override and no cache root. It uses fixed public prompts and no consumer data. It reads a local model directory, computes the weight hash via WeightHasher, and prints JSON containing generated tokens. No network, coordinator, key or attestation surfaces are touched. It rejects mimo_v2 models and bounds the inputs (batch size 1-64, maxTokens up to 131072). Sessions are shut down on both the success and error paths. I did not identify a concrete security regression. Remaining questions: confirm the ProviderBenchmark target is not shipped in the signed production artifact or CLI, and review the submodule diff for the MTP carry and chained-decode state.
